title: Copy Any Clearance: CRAFT
hook: Clearance delivery talks at 200 words a minute. Here's how you win.

scenes.narration: Engine's running at Mercer Field, pad on your knee, and you key up clearance delivery. The controller inhales once and starts talking. Alright kid — here's how you never miss a word.
Before they talk — what's the FIRST item every I F R clearance starts with? Commit.
onScreenText: What comes FIRST in every clearance?

scenes.narration: Clearance limit — usually your destination. Then route. Then altitude. Then frequency. Then transponder. Five items: C R A F T.
Why the same order every time? So you can write C R A F T down the page BEFORE you call. Now you're filling in blanks, not chasing a stranger's sentences. Standardization is the safety feature, kid.
One trap. 'Cleared as filed' covers the route only — the altitude, frequency, and squawk are still coming. Read it all back. The F A A loves an acronym the way a consultant loves a framework.
Eyes closed. All five items, in order, out loud. I'll wait.
Clearance limit. Route. Altitude. Frequency. Transponder. The one craft project that keeps you out of a mountain.
A I M four dash four dash three. Go read it.

quiz.question: You call clearance delivery at Mercer Field. The FIRST item of the clearance will be:
quiz.explanation: Every IFR clearance starts with the clearance limit — usually your destination airport. (AIM 4-4-3)

quiz.question: You hear "cleared to Denver as filed." What should you still expect to copy?
quiz.explanation: "As filed" covers the route only. The A, F, and T of CRAFT — altitude, frequency, transponder — are still coming.

quiz.question: Why write C-R-A-F-T on your pad before calling clearance delivery?
choices: Clearances follow that exact order, so you just fill in blanks
ATC will ask you to read the letters back
quiz.explanation: Clearance items are issued in a standard order (AIM 4-4-3). Pre-writing CRAFT turns a fast readback into a fill-in-the-blank.
